DEF-180.title: In-page vendor placement signals in OpenRTB envelopes lack format tagging
DEF-180.expected: The project-documented widget/zone and bid.ext in-page dialect can be identified as vendor in-page content even when carried in an OpenRTB envelope. Standard OpenRTB requires a media object, so imp.format_required for these bare widget impressions is correct and remains asserted.
DEF-180.actual: Format detection does not tag these imp/seatbid-shaped widget examples as inpage: format-detect.js rule 5 reads the ext.widget_id/zone_id placement signal only for the JSON-feed single-object/array shape and is gated off whenever the payload is already imp[]/seatbid[]-shaped. The adm-bearing control renders its markup correctly. The request media-object error is not an implementation deviation.
notes: This is a vendor capability distinction, not proof that media-free impressions comply with IAB OpenRTB. The earlier reading of conditional Imp field-table entries was incomplete; section 3.1 explicitly requires a media object.
Only missing vendor tagging and case-specific creative identity failures remain pinned. Response-dialect validation and baseline request rejection are asserted independently.
Coverage-closure cases extend this existing group; exact additional signatures and measured browser evidence are recorded per case, not counted as independent new defects.

2026-09-08 (feature 029): the preview half of this record is CLOSED. public/ortbtools.app.js now resolves the bid.ext carrier through the In-Page Push dialect's own alias table and renders the card, so all five carrier cases measure kind=push, rendered=partial and a visible headline marker; their preview.kind, preview.rendered and identity signatures are retired and expect.preview.capabilityGap is cleared. Only the format-tagging line remains on each case, and it is Core work.
